mathematical_contract.degree_extension: The one rational multi-affine factor package accepts axis coefficient counts four through six. A quintic split produces one proved linear-axis factor and an exact quartic quotient; no degree-specific positive assertion is added.
mathematical_contract.slice_authority: Exact rational specializations and signed maximal minors only propose bilinear slice factors. Exact Hypersolve division remains the authority for accepting each slice divisor.
mathematical_contract.fourth_sample_rejection: A factor reconstructed from any three exact roots predicts the fourth specialized root whenever its specialized axis coefficient is nonzero. Absence from a nonempty exact root set rejects the proposal; an empty or undecidable root set makes no negative claim.
mathematical_contract.lift: Both retained-coordinate orientations use the existing translated first-Taylor/highest-slice proof, with exact two-anchor projective alignment retained for repeated factors. Every candidate must still divide the complete tensor exactly.
mathematical_contract.axis_scheduling: For quintic axes only, exact nonzero counts in the leading slice order equally sized axes from denser to sparser. This can avoid accidental specialization degree drops, but it is scheduling evidence only: unknown signs score zero and the selected axis supplies no mathematical claim.
mathematical_contract.selected_sign: The verified linear factor and exact quartic quotient enter the same bounded recursive sign authority. A selected zero factor proves the product zero; decided nonzero signs multiply exactly.
mathematical_contract.resource_bound: Dimensions are checked and all bivariate products and reconstructed tensors retain the 16384-control ceiling. The recursive split budget is four, sufficient for the supported quintic decomposition and no higher.
mathematical_contract.policy: A supportable rational quintic factorization is Certified under STRICT and APPROXIMATE_512 without terminal consumption. The sextic control remains Predicate uncertainty in STRICT and returns Zero only after APPROXIMATE_512 records Approximate512Consumed.
mathematical_contract.failure: Missing exact rational roots, unresolved exact signs, failed slice or full-tensor division, degenerate lift relations, unsupported coefficient towers, resource overflow, or exhaustion of the four-split budget makes no exact claim and falls through to the shared policy terminal. No tolerance, sampled positive assertion, compatibility shim, or second Boolean engine is introduced.

capability.comparison_revision: The product of the selected-zero exact quartic fixture and another positive coupled multi-affine factor was unsupported. STRICT returned Predicate uncertainty and APPROXIMATE_512 consumed its terminal.
capability.source_revision: One rational multi-affine quintic factor is reconstructed from exact slice divisors, lifted and proved by exact complete-tensor division, and recursively signed with its quartic quotient.
capability.certified_fixture: The formerly terminal quintic rational three-field fixture returns Certified Zero under STRICT and APPROXIMATE_512; neither policy consumes the approximate terminal.
capability.differential_factor_coverage: Five distinct dense multi-affine factors reconstruct on every axis; F^2*G^2*H multiplicity reconstructs on every axis; one rational factor is recovered with a quartic cofactor; an unfactored quintic is rejected.
capability.remaining_policy_control: Multiplying the exact quartic fixture by two additional positive coupled factors makes every axis sextic. The bounded package deliberately declines it; STRICT remains explicitly uncertain and APPROXIMATE_512 returns Zero only with Approximate512Consumed.
capability.remaining_exactness_boundary: Recover bounded sextic factors or construct another exact selected-root relation only after axis content, linear resultant, binary selected-root, quadratic, repeated-cubic, rational square-free-cubic, rational quartic, and rational quintic paths fail.

benchmark.primary_method: all-feature release unit-test and comparative executables pinned to CPU 11; exact fully-qualified filters; seven perf-stat repetitions for focused fixtures and three for fixed-work controls; median retired instructions and branches are primary

stable_axis_optimization.interpretation: Trying the densest exact leading slice first selects a stable factorization axis and avoids a deeper positive-factor quotient chain. The scheduling cut repays about one fifth of deterministic work and allocations at a visible 0.07 MiB peak-live-heap cost.

sextic_coupled_terminal.strict_result: Predicate uncertainty with no approximate consumption
sextic_coupled_terminal.interpretation: Sextic coupled tensors are the next exactness and dominant-work boundary; this control proves the terminal remains selected by policy rather than unconditional.

fixed_work_historical_controls.method: matched 38a8b57 and 2d26334 all-feature release comparative executables against identical dependency revisions, pinned to CPU 11; three complete perf-stat repetitions; fixture construction excluded from timed loops
fixed_work_historical_controls.interpretation: Both ordinary production lanes are instruction- and branch-neutral. The cold quintic package therefore consumes no measurable hot-path regression budget.

competitive_context.method: final all-feature release comparative executable pinned to CPU 11; 11 complete samples at a 100 ms target; fixture construction excluded; retired-instruction controls are primary because the shared host was visibly loaded
competitive_context.interpretation: Cavalier and Curvo remain throughput targets rather than exactness peers. The unusually wide wall-time ranges are retained rather than normalized away; deterministic fixed-work controls show the quintic cut does not enter either lane.
